   Typhoon Champi sweeps past Taiwan, one dead and 500 injured

 Set as preferred source Listen Summarise Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan, killing one man and injuring 527 people. It brought strong winds, heavy rain, fallen trees and power cuts, Reuters said.
 The storm weakened as it moved north. Taiwan's CWA said it was about 150km east of the island, with gusts near 126kmh, and it was heading towards China and southern Japan.
 Taiwan closed offices and schools for a second day in the north and centre, including Taipei. More than 167,000 homes lost power at one point, and 242 flights were cancelled.

 TAIPEI – Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Oct 24 killing one person and injuring more than 500, downing trees and severing power, as it continues to weaken and head north towards the Chinese coast.
 At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific in 2026 , Champi is weakening though still packing gusts of around 126kmh near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA).
 The storm was about 150km east of Taiwan, the CWA said, having glanced the island’s north-east coast in the early hours of Oct 24 .
 The storm's forecast track shows it is now turning north toward the Chinese coast and eventually move into southern Japan.
 Taiwan's fire department said the death toll remaining at one, a man swept away by waves from the island of Liuqiu, with 527 injuries during the heavy wind and torrential rain.
 Taipower said at one point more than 167,000 homes had lost electricity, though most had been reconnected.
 The transport ministry said 242 flights were cancelled, though that was an improvement from Oct 23, when the number was almost 1,000 .
 In the capital Taipei, there were downed trees and on-off squally rain showers.
 A swathe of northern and central Taiwan, including Taipei, declared a second day of office and school closures on Oct 24 .
 Taiwan is generally very well-prepared for typhoons, which keeps casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn too. REUTERS
